title: 1963 AHSME Problem 10
statement: Point \(P\) is taken interior to a square with side-length \(a\) and such that it is equally distant from two consecutive vertices and from the side opposite these vertices. If \(d\) represents the common distance, then \(d\) equals:

solutions.text:
Place the opposite side at height \(0\) and the two vertices at height \(a.\) Then \(P=(\frac{a}{2},d).\) Equality of the vertex distance and \(d\) gives \[\left(\frac a2\right)^2+(a-d)^2=d^2,\] so \(\frac{5a^2}{4}=2ad\) and \(d=\frac{5a}{8}.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The equal distances to two consecutive vertices put \(P\) on their perpendicular bisector
If the distance to the opposite side is \(d,\) use a right triangle with legs \(\frac{a}{2}\) and \(a-d\)
